text.p: The Israeli shekel closed almost unchanged against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies in active and mixed trading, dealers said.
"Trading was very active today and in early trading the shekel weakened slightly against the dollar following the dollar's rise abroad," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi.
"The Bank of Israel was not seen in the market today despite the fact that after the setting of the representative rate the basket fell to 7.05 percent below the slope," he said.

"Trading was very mixed today. The session opened with some demand for the dollar but towards the end of the trading day the trend changed and the shekel closed almost unchanged," said another dealer.

The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of 7.0 percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at 6.0 percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band, the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1690 against 3.1680 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5464 shekels against 3.5463 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8801 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8761 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.0946 shekels per mark against 2.0971 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1670 shekels.
